title: Stoquastic frustration-free constraint satisfaction

problem.name: Stoquastic k-SAT
problem.statement_latex: Given $H=\sum_{a=1}^m H_a$ on $n$ qubits, with each positive semidefinite $H_a$ acting on at most $k=O(1)$ qubits and having real nonpositive off-diagonal entries, distinguish $\lambda_{\min}(H)=0$ from $\lambda_{\min}(H)\ge1/\operatorname{poly}(n)$. Zero energy means that the local constraints share a zero vector. Complexity is measured in classical running time and quantum evolution time or simulation gates, with the path and spectral-gap promises specified below.
problem.statement_text: Given $H=\sum_{a=1}^m H_a$ on $n$ qubits, with each positive semidefinite $H_a$ acting on at most $k=O(1)$ qubits and having real nonpositive off-diagonal entries, distinguish $\lambda_{\min}(H)=0$ from $\lambda_{\min}(H)\ge1/\operatorname{poly}(n)$. Complexity is measured in classical running time and quantum evolution time or simulation gates, with the path and spectral-gap promises specified below.

quantum.headline_latex: Polynomial evolution time for a suitably gapped, initialized path, stoquastic frustration-free adiabatic evolution.
quantum.details_latex: The polynomial guarantee uses the smoothness, inverse-polynomial gap and initialization assumptions (A0)--(A3) of Bravyi--Terhal. For unrestricted instances, stoquastic 6-SAT is MA-complete: a polynomial-time quantum solution would imply $\mathrm{MA}\subseteq\mathrm{BQP}$ and hence $\mathrm{NP}\subseteq\mathrm{BQP}$.
quantum.headline_text: Polynomial evolution time for a suitably gapped, initialized path, stoquastic frustration-free adiabatic evolution.
quantum.details_text: The polynomial guarantee uses the smoothness, inverse-polynomial gap and initialization assumptions (A0)–(A3) of Bravyi–Terhal. For unrestricted instances, stoquastic 6-SAT is MA-complete: a polynomial-time quantum solution would imply $\mathrm{MA}\subseteq\mathrm{BQP}$ and hence $\mathrm{NP}\subseteq\mathrm{BQP}$.

classical.headline_latex: $\operatorname{poly}(n,\delta^{-1})$ time, Bravyi--Terhal sampling under the same path assumptions.
classical.details_latex: The simulator samples a distribution within total variation distance $\delta$ of the final ground-state measurement distribution. Its nonnegative-amplitude random walks track the path. Stoquastic $k$-SAT is in MA for each fixed $k$, with a classical randomized polynomial-time witness verifier.
